components.css: .ds-card { background-color: var(--mui-palette-background-paper, #121212); background-image: var(--mui-overlays-1, linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0.05), rgba(255,255,255,0.05))); color: var(--mui-palette-text-primary, #fff); border-radius: 4px; padding: 16px 16px 24px; box-shadow: 0px 2px 1px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.2), 0px 1px 1px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.14), 0px 1px 3px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.12); font-family: Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0 0 8px; text-align: center; font-size: 2.125rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.235; letter-spacing: 0.00735em; } .ds-triad { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-evenly; gap: 32px; } .ds-field { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.5; letter-spacing: 0.00938em; } .ds-field-label { text-decoration: underline dotted; } .ds-field-value { cursor: pointer; border-bottom: 1px dashed transparent; } .ds-field-value:hover, .ds-field-value:focus-visible { border-bottom-color: var(--mui-palette-text-secondary, rgba(255,255,255,0.7)); outline: none; } .ds-gauge { width: 140px; height: 4px; overflow: hidden; margin: 2px 0 8px; } .ds-gauge span { display: block; height: 100%; } .ds-gauge-sante { background: #7a211b; } .ds-gauge-sante span { background: var(--mui-palette-error-main, #f44336); } .ds-gauge-equilibre { background: #145b7b; } .ds-gauge-equilibre span { background: var(--mui-palette-info-main, #29b6f6); } .ds-gauge-eclat { background: #7f5313; } .ds-gauge-eclat span { background: var(--mui-palette-warning-main, #ffa726); }

narrative.overview:
The sheet should be immersive, customisable and alive. It should feel like being inside the character, not like filling in a form. Everything visible today is a provisional base: Material UI v9 with its default theme, dark by default. It's documented here so that new screens stay consistent until Oniria gets its own identity. When that identity arrives, it goes through the theme (createTheme in src/app/providers.tsx), not through one-off overrides scattered across components.

The confirmed feel is feutré et immersif, avec une dose de vivant et réactif (muted and immersive, with a touch of lively and reactive). Surfaces stay calm, dark and low-contrast at rest. The liveliness shows up when you interact: each segment of an XP bar brightens on hover and gives its value in a tooltip; a lock tells you whether a part of the sheet is frozen or still free; editable values reveal a dashed underline; every save is answered with a toast.

The game's structure organises the screen. Computed groups (Caractères, Facultés, Existences, Expérience) are cards with a large centred title. Inside them, the game's triads (Corps / Esprit / Âme, Chair / Pensée / Lien, Santé / Équilibre / Éclat, Éprouver / Apprendre / Vivre) sit in three columns. Lists the player maintains (traits, Corpus, weapons, objects) are compact tables with a left-aligned title and an "Ajouter…" button underneath. Game meanings are carried by MUI's six semantic palette roles, never by custom colours.
keyCharacteristics: Stock MUI v9 theme with CSS variables; dark ("Sombre") by default, plus "Clair" and "Système" modes chosen by the player.
Single centred column up to 1400px wide. Tab panels stack below 900px and sit side by side above it.
Typographic hierarchy that mirrors the game: section card → triad group or list → stat line.
Quiet editing: values look like plain text with a faint pencil, are saved on Enter or blur, and cancelled with Escape.
Game states expressed through the palette roles (error, info, warning, success, secondary) and the lock.
Depth in dark mode comes from MUI's white overlays, not from shadows.

rules.name: The Palette-Role Rule
rules.body: Game meanings use only the theme's semantic roles (error, info, warning, success, secondary, primary), written as color="warning" or 'error.main', never as a hex value. This is what keeps Santé, Équilibre and Éclat correct in Clair mode (#d32f2f, #0288d1, #ed6c02) without extra code.

rules.name: The Warning-Means-Unsettled Rule
rules.body: Apart from the Éclat gauge, orange always means "not settled yet": free to change, waiting for validation, or about to cost something irreversible. A validated, settled state is neutral grey (the closed lock, the "Validée" chip).

rules.name: The Game Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Typographic roles follow the game, not the page: a centred Title = a computed section of the sheet; a Subtitle = a triad group, or a list the player maintains; Body = one stat. Don't use Title or Subtitle for anything else.

rules.name: The Overlay-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: In dark mode, convey depth through elevation (which drives the overlay), never through custom shadows or hand-picked greys. A hard-coded #1e1e1e card is correct in Sombre and wrong in Clair.

dos: Do take every colour, radius and space from the MUI theme (theme.vars.palette.*, theme.spacing, shape.borderRadius 4px). The base is provisional, so the theme is the single place where Oniria's identity will be set.

Do reuse the established game mappings: Santé error, Équilibre info, Éclat warning; skill degrees Base primary, Principe secondary, Maîtrise and Technique success, Enchaînement warning; history entries Attribution success, Dépense primary, Remboursement info, XP perdue warning, Offert secondary.
Do mark anything unsettled (free to change, waiting for validation, about to cost XP irreversibly) with warning, and settled states with neutral grey.
Do check every new screen in Sombre, Clair and Système, and at mobile width, where tab panels stack and triads wrap.
Do keep the Label : valeur / max stat line, attach rules text and formulas as a tooltip on a dotted-underlined label, and show the XP cost in the label of any button that spends it.
Do build new lists with CollectionTable (small table, inline-edit cells, delete icon, "+ Ajouter…" underneath, a one-line empty state), and let wide tables scroll inside their card.
Do keep surfaces calm at rest and put the liveliness in interaction: hover, focus, edit, save, and tooltips that reveal values.
donts: Don't treat stock MUI as Oniria's identity, and don't polish it piece by piece. It is a confirmed provisional base, and the identity will be defined as a whole, in the theme.
Don't hard-code white, black, rgba(255,255,255,…) or hex values in components. They break Clair mode. LoadingButton still does this.
Don't introduce a new colour for a game meaning. Map it to an existing palette role, or wait for the theme-level identity.
Don't let a player spend or lose XP without a dialog that shows the split, or delete anything without a confirmation that names the consequence.
Don't rely on Roboto's or Inter's metrics until the font stack is fixed in the theme.
